correctness.rationale: Every auxiliary interval hit set has a unique canonical pair (minimum marked right endpoint, maximum marked left endpoint), allowing at most 1+m+binom(m,2)-c intersection traces. Extremal right/left marked vertices duplicate two query traces, unless they coincide, in which case all m-1 other intervals contain that one; this yields B+m-2 for m>=3 and forces zero containments. Contiguous-block singleton realizability eliminates nonconsecutive overlap; all m-2 interior self-deleted profiles force neighboring overlaps, giving a path. Exact interval probes J_[i,j]=[4i+3,4j+3] prove attainability; duplicate m=3 endpoint profiles force nine vertices. Base cases 1,2 and VC consequences checked. Generic perturbations preserve finite interval intersection adjacency. verify.py exhausts abstract endpoint matchings m<=6 and constructs m<=10, not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: Quantifier-free adjacency types are the base layer of finite-model parameter counting. The sharp quadratic coefficient, exact path rigidity, and minimum-order exceptional case distinguish open from closed neighborhoods and supply smallest testing models for all realized unary trace profiles; m=3 versus m=4 identifies the exact shattering frontier. These are natural universal invariants with explicit constructions and a nontrivial diagonal correction, not a numerically arbitrary slice.
